instruction: Inspect the supplied FastAPI user-service repository and produce an implementation plan for adding durable HTTP idempotency to POST /api/users/. Clients may send an optional Idempotency-Key header. The first request must create the user normally; replaying the same key with the same canonical payload must return the original status and response without creating another user; reusing the key with a different payload must return HTTP 409. The behaviour must survive process restarts and concurrent duplicate requests. Requests without the header must retain existing behaviour. Cover data model and transaction boundaries, payload fingerprinting, concurrency and failure recovery, compatibility, public and protected tests, observability, security/abuse limits, staged rollout and rollback. Identify relevant existing files and give an ordered implementation and validation plan. Do not modify the repository.

rubric.description: Identifies the relevant router, SQLAlchemy model/session, schema, and test files and grounds the plan in the supplied repository.
Defines exact behaviour for first use, identical replay, conflicting payload, missing header, status code, and stored response.
Proposes a durable idempotency record with key, canonical payload fingerprint, response/status, lifecycle fields, and appropriate constraints.
Defines an atomic transaction or reservation strategy that prevents duplicate users under concurrent requests and explains recovery from in-progress or failed work.
Specifies deterministic public and protected tests for replay, conflict, restart persistence, concurrency, regression, and documentation.
Covers metrics, structured logs, abuse/key limits, retention or cleanup, staged rollout, validation, and rollback.
